subject: Request: seller ID split causing GCP marketplace VAT mismatch
messages:
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@acmecloud.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GCP marketplace invoice — seller ID split causing VAT allocation issue

Hi Grace / Marissa,

Thanks for taking a look. We discovered a recurring discrepancy between the GCP Marketplace invoices and our internal usage ledger for July. Two meter lines were billed under different seller IDs in the marketplace export (seller_uk_112 vs seller_eu_44) but should have been consolidated under seller_eu_44 for VAT reporting. That split caused our AP team to withhold EU VAT on one line and apply UK VAT on the other — creating a tax mismatch when reconciling to our accounting system.

Attached: acme_usage_export_202607.csv (raw marketplace export) and a compressed GCP invoice snippet. Can you confirm if Redwood can: 
- map the two seller IDs to a single merchant entity on your side,
- reissue a credit/charge to correct the VAT distribution, and
- provide a short evidence package we can file for our auditors?

We're under a month-end closing window in early September and need the adjustment before 2026-09-30 to avoid a complex VAT re-proc. If you need a sample of our ledger join or a preferred format, let me know.

Thanks,
Sasha
Sasha Ivanov
Billing Ops Manager, ACME Cloud
billing-team@acmecloud.com

Subject: Re: GCP marketplace invoice — seller ID split causing VAT allocation issue

Hi Sasha — thanks for the details and the export. I've looped in Marissa and Jonas from finance so we can run a mapping pass. Quick notes: 

- We can run a reconciliation join on the marketplace usage_id + timestamp to find rows that migrated between seller IDs.
- To reissue a credit memo we need the original marketplace invoice numbers and the buyer legal entity (we got ACME Cloud but please confirm exact billing entity name/registration).
- For auditor evidence, we typically provide: (1) original marketplace export, (2) our join script and mapping table, and (3) the credit memo + ledger journal entry.

Can you attach the invoice PDF(s) for July and confirm the buyer legal name (as on the invoice) so we can draft the credit memo? Also, which currency/VAT regime should we show on the corrected line (GBP vs EUR)? If it's EUR for both lines we'll route to our EU tax team.

I'll assign a tracking ticket and aim to have a preliminary mapping by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0199

Attachment requested: invoice PDFs (July 2026)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GCP marketplace invoice — seller ID split causing VAT allocation issue

Grace/Marissa — I pulled the marketplace export and ran an initial join against our internal metering table. Findings so far (high level):

- There are ~1,200 usage rows in July where the usage_key matches but seller_id differs. Roughly 78% of the token volume is under seller_eu_44 (expected) and 22% under seller_uk_112 (outlier).
- The outlier rows share the same product SKU and timestamps (within 1–2 minutes), which points to a listing attribution bug during a cross-region migration.

Action items I propose:
1) Create a mapping table that consolidates seller_uk_112 -> seller_eu_44 for the affected usage_ids and generate a corrected invoice line set.
2) Draft a credit memo for the UK-attributed lines and corresponding debit on the EU line so net amount is unchanged but VAT reallocation occurs.
3) Produce an evidence packet (CSV joins, mapping_draft.xlsx, and the SQL we ran) for ACME's auditors.

I'm attaching sellerid_mapping_draft.xlsx and the SQL snippet. Once Sasha confirms the buyer legal name and the invoice PDFs, I'll finish the credit memo draft.

Jonas Weber
Senior Accountant, Revenue Recognition
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Thanks, everyone — appreciate the quick triage.

Confirming buyer legal name: ACME Cloud Services Ltd (VAT: GB999999999). July invoice PDFs attached in this reply for reference. We'd prefer the corrected VAT to show EUR where applicable (line-level currency on the corrected EU line). ACME can accept a credit memo issued by Redwood dated no later than 2026-09-30.

Please proceed with the mapping and let us know when the draft credit memo is ready so we can route to our tax team. If you want, we can run a double-check on our side once you share the mapping CSV.
